service.description: Start a request the current user makes with their own reference (clientRef, ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$) of serviceName (a service or an operation, as the caller names it). A reference already used answers duplicate true with the result stored for it (store#ClientRequest): the caller answers that and does nothing else. Otherwise the reference is claimed in the caller's transaction, so a second try that overlaps the first waits for it and then fails (the client tries again and gets the duplicate), and a request that fails leaves no claim. Call store#ClientRequest with the result in the same transaction. The reference is keyed by user and serviceName alone, not by the parameters: a client gives each request its own ref, and the same ref with other parameters answers the first request's result. A ref is kept client_request_keep_days (30): sent again after that, the request runs again.

Keep what a request claimed by claim#ClientRequest answered, as JSON (dates as milliseconds), in the request's transaction: a retry with the same clientRef gets it with duplicate true. An answer over 256 KB is kept empty (the retry answers duplicate true alone).

Call serviceName with parameters once per clientRef of the current user: the first call runs it and keeps its answer (claim#ClientRequest, store#ClientRequest, in this transaction); a call again with the same clientRef answers that with duplicate true and does nothing. With no clientRef the service just runs. For the screens' transitions of mutations a client may queue (Chat's edit, redact, react, votePoll, markRead); the service runs as the user, with its own checks.
The daily job: the clientRefs older than days (the property client_request_keep_days, 30 by default) go, so a client's retry is answered as a duplicate for that long.

actions.script: const keep = Math.max(1, Number(days || System.getProperty('client_request_keep_days') || 30)) const before = Number(ec.user.nowTimestamp) - keep * 86400000 removedCount = Number(ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.client.ClientRequestRef').condition('createdDate', 'less', String(before)) .disableAuthz().deleteAll() || 0)

service.description:
One chunk of a file the current user sends in parts (ClientUpload): uploadId, the client's own name of the upload (^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{1,64}$); offset, where the chunk starts; total, the file's size (at most 25 MB); fileName and contentType of the file; chunk, the bytes (a file part). The chunk is taken only at the offset of the bytes held: one at another offset (a chunk sent again after a lost answer, or one past a gap) is not taken and accepted is false; received always says how many bytes are held, so the client goes on from there. The chunk that ends at total joins the file (complete true); the attachment services take it by uploadId. A chunk of a complete upload changes nothing (complete true). A total other than the upload's, or a chunk past it, is an error.
Limits: a chunk other than the last is at least client_upload_min_chunk_bytes (256 KB by default); a user has at most client_upload_max_count (20) uploads not complete, of client_upload_max_mb (100) MB in all, so a new one past them is refused until one finishes or expires. The join reads the chunks one at a time into the file's buffer, so the heap holds the file once and a chunk.

How much of the current user's upload uploadId the server holds: received bytes of total, and complete once the file is joined. found is false for an upload the server does not have (never started, or expired): the client starts it again from offset 0.

actions.script: found = false; received = 0; total = null; complete = false; fileName = null if (!ec.user.userId) { ec.message.addError('No user'); return } const row = ec.entity.find('moqui.basic.client.ClientUpload').condition({userId: ec.user.userId, uploadId: String(uploadId)}).disableAuthz().one() if (!row) return found = true received = Number(row.receivedSize || 0) total = Number(row.totalSize || 0) complete = row.completedDate != null fileName = row.fileName ?? null

service.description: Internal, for the attachment services that take a file by uploadId: the current user's complete upload, its file's location, fileName, contentType and fileSize. An upload of another user, or one not complete, is an error. It stays until it expires (clean#ClientUploads), so an attachment sent again after a lost answer finds it.

The hourly job: uploads with no chunk for hours (the property client_upload_expire_hours, 24 by default), finished or not, go with their files (remove#ClientUpload), and a user's upload folder left empty goes too. Each upload is on its own, in its own transaction: one that cannot be removed is logged and the rest go on.
Internal, for clean#ClientUploads (authorization disabled): one upload's row and its files.
